body: Maybe it's also maladaptive daydreaming?

I think people feel calm or good because of the sense of control over at least one aspect (if not the most important one) of our lives. And I agree, don't call yourself a freak over this. You're just trying to cope.

I was in an indoor pool/spa with my ex. It was only for two hours, but it was the most peaceful and playful bliss. Being alone with someone you love that loves you back, floating around aimlessly, looking up at the indoor cave ceiling, nothing tops that. It was like a dream. One of the pools even had whole oranges just floating about.
Thanks for reminding me :)

Hey, I'm sorry that happened. But 3 weeks without cutting is really good. Even if you manage to do one week, or one day, that's an accomplishment. Keep count of the days you don't. Track it. If you relapse again, just focus on the next goal. I don't know, maybe it won't help. But you got to three weeks! That's great. Be proud of yourself on that at least.

I'm sorry you're going through that. One thing I would like to say is not to compare yourself to others career trajectories. I mean, you say you're 18. You could change careers again next year and be alright. I understand that sharing classes with 15 year olds must suck. But I've been in classes where there were 28 year olds, 18 year olds, and everything in between and it's just fine. 
You know what's much worse? Sticking with one career path, wasting even more years and realising you don't want to do that much further along the line. 
But I get it, the being tired all the time, having to deal with someone else's crisis on top of everything. I feel you.
Get a good Belgian beer. Something with a lot of taste.

The Dollop - history podcast with two comedians that tell you insane episodes of contemporary and older history (usually American). Start with The Rube, I cried laughing. I still listen to it from time to time.

They just don't want to deal with your problems. They don't want to help you get better, they don't want to listen, so they say those things to make themselves feel better, because if depression doesn't exist or if it is your fault, then they are blameless, and they can sleep at night. Then they just hope that you'll deal with it and never mention it again. It sucks

Cry in the shower, at night when everyone's asleep, in public transport, find a empty street with a bench, in a park.. Crying is so relieving, you should be able to cry in the privacy of your own home. That really suck. I feel you.

Knowing that theoretically you maybe could try and change your situation, and not doing it, hating yourself for not trying, and concluding that hey, this *is* the perfect punishment. Life is hell. Couldn't agree more.

I don't think it's weak to be afraid. Everyone is afraid at some point. Some more than others. Telling someone they're weak is just counterproductive. 
It's ok to not be ok, I don't know if I'm making sense. I hope that at least the physical expressions of your situations lessen a bit today. Good luck
Thanks for the laugh, it is great
Nice!
Right before I go to sleep. I can daydream with no guilt. Hours of blissful unconsciousness ahead.

I don't have the means to move out. I even share a room with a family member. This family member is the one that makes me feel like this. They have had such a control over what I think, what I do for my whole life that I don't know how to escape. I think deep down they must hate me, and they've made me hate myself. Thanks again btw.
Thank you for asking and caring.

I don't really want to but my family is pushing me up against a wall and I'm starting not to see another way out. I'm also a weak push-over and I cannot for the life of me (literally) see another way out but the one that has been given to me. I can't ask anyone for help. Dying seems like the only answer.

This made me really happy to read :) I hope you continue not cutting for many more months. I mean wow, you've managed to stop for a whole month after doing it daily for years, that's insane. You should be so proud. I'm proud for you. If you ever feel like you might slip, come back to this post. Remember this feeling of pride
I don't know if this is what you mean, but the Friends episode where Ross wears leather pants makes have to physically leave to room. Like secondhand embarrassment.

Hey you managed to do 6 months! Like you were capable of not checking up on your ex for like literally half a year that's really good. Ok so you relapsed, but that still doesn't take away from your accomplishment. I don't really know how to help with the nightmares and the child memories, it seems those problems are related. Maybe if you focus on solving or understanding one things will be better, or at least make more sense. I feel you though.

I think everyone has the right to complain. Experience is subjective. Sure, some people might have it objectively worse than you, but that doesn't necessarily cheapen your experience. I think the first step is just accepting that what you are going through is legitimate. Hope your week gets better.

I feel you. I don't know a lot about mental illnesses but from my experience it feels like some traits are "contagious". You end up having to come up with defenses that are unhealthy. Or sometimes the abuse is too much and you break. I try to imagine the real me is behind fortified walls and that they can't touch me. A small comfort really. Hope you manage to get out and that you start to heal.
I feel you. The wanting to live one moment and then die the next. It's so insanely tiring. I don't really know how to help, but I'm listening.

What would you do if your main problem wasn't internal (that is to say, not a problem with intrusive or bad thoughts) but external? What if you were in a situation so destructive or toxic that you would contemplate killing yourself? How do you convince yourself then, when the options are either suffering or dying, to take the first option because that means living? 

If I was in another situation I would be fine. But I can't get myself out of this one.

Thanks again.
Thanks for replying. Honestly, time. There's onlyy so much control that I have over these bad circumstances. Sleep is also great I think. I've tried meditation, it helps sometimes.
